definitions.explanation: The craft of making or altering clothing, or the quality/style of how a garment is made.
The way something is prepared, arranged, or presented. Used for how things are organized or made to appear.

examples.japanese: この{服|ふく}は{仕立|した}てがいい。
スーツをオーダーメイドで{仕立|した}てた。
{母|はは}は{着物|きもの}の{仕立|した}てを{長年|ながねん}やっている。
examples.english: My mother has been doing kimono tailoring for many years.

examples.japanese: クイズ{仕立|した}ての{番組|ばんぐみ}だ。
examples.english: It's a program set up in a quiz format.

examples.japanese: {物語|ものがたり}{仕立|した}てで{歴史|れきし}を{紹介|しょうかい}する。
examples.english: Introduce history in a narrative format.

examples.japanese: ミステリー{仕立|した}ての{映画|えいが}で、{最後|さいご}まで{犯人|はんにん}がわからなかった。
examples.english: It was a movie done in a mystery style, and I couldn't figure out the culprit until the end.

notes:
The verb form is {仕立|した}てる (to tailor, to make up). The noun {仕立|した}て refers to the result or quality of the making.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕立|した}てがいい (well-tailored)
- {仕立|した}て{屋|や} (tailor, dressmaker)
- オーダーメイドの{仕立|した}て (custom tailoring)
- 〜{仕立|した}て (in the style of ~, formatted as ~)

Sense 2 is used as a suffix: 〜{仕立|した}て means "done in the style of" or "set up as." This usage is common in entertainment, publishing, and food descriptions (e.g., {洋風|ようふう}{仕立|した}て, Western-style preparation).
